request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Retiring a person is in, and all 4 tests in the spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

**What it does now:**
- **Retiring:** each person's row has a "Retire from" date and a Retire button. A blank date means the sheet's today. A person counts as retired as soon as a date is set, even one after today. Their row shows Retired "yes" and the date under Retired from; everyone else shows "no" and a blank date.
- **Audit:** retiring writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> from=<date>`. It adds no rollup line, because no totals change.
- **Claims after retirement:** a claim dated after the retirement date is refused with an error, both on the screen and on the server. This covers adding, editing and quick add. Claims dated on or before the date are still allowed, even if added later.
- **Show retired:** a checkbox on the screen, off when the screen first opens and unchanged by loading a sheet. While it's off, retired people get no row at all. Their claims still count in every total.
- **Stored data:** a new database migration, `V16__person_retired.sql`, adds a nullable `retired_from` date column to people.

**Behaviour I chose where the request was silent:**
- Retiring someone who is already retired replaces their date with the new one.
- A retired person can still be edited and can still have statements taken.
- There is no "unretire" action.
- If you have a person's editor open and you retire that same person, your save still goes through rather than being refused as out of date, since you made both changes.

The server changes are mainly in `PersonService.retire` and `ClaimService.refuseAfterRetirement`; the screen changes are in `people.ts` and `claims.ts`.
